target_customer: Health plans, health systems and medicare patients with COPD and chronic lung disease
problem: Pulmonary rehab is hard to access, leading to hospitalizations.
business_model: Reimbursed virtual care billed to Medicare, Medicaid and commercial plans

founders.name: Vaughn Koch
previous_startups: Movity (exited to Trulia, per YC page)

competitors.name: Wellinks
competitors.what: Virtual COPD program with connected devices, coaching and virtual pulmonary rehab
competitors.traction_then: Partnered with Highmark BCBS Delaware in June 2023

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth video, device kits and billing; operational and clinical delivery rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: Payer contracts, referral relationships and reimbursement coverage take time to build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Optum Arcadia partnered with Kivo in April 2026 rather than copying.

market_need_then: Pulmonary rehab is covered by Medicare for COPD but access is poor; Kivo reports 8k dollars per patient payer savings (company claim).

identity.visual_style: Clean modern with patient video testimonials
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and encouraging ('Break free from COPD')

brand_strength.rationale: No brand-focused press; trade coverage is about funding and partnerships.

outcome_analysis: Kivo Health is active with about 40 staff and a 10 million dollar Series A in October 2026 that brings total funding above 16 million per trade press. Partnerships with Stanford, UCLA-affiliated referrers, Optum Arcadia and Priority Health show payer and system traction. A physician CEO and reimbursable service helped. Earlier rounds are not itemized in sources, so history is partial.
notes: Series A confirmed by Axios, MobiHealthNews, GeekWire. Earlier funding of about 500K (pre-seed, YC, Liquid 2 Ventures) is aggregator-only and unverified. Some aggregators give a conflicting Durham NC location and different founders; ignored as likely a different company. Wellinks funding date not verified. Founded 2021 per one profile; UCLA study covers patients from Oct 2022. NuvoAir is another virtual COPD player but no dated source was found, so it is omitted.
